FACTS: episodes/_planning/EP64_memphis_FACTS_LEDGER.v001.md (WRITTEN 2026-08-04, RECOUNTED 2026-08-04: 123 fact lines, 110 verbatim, 12 quarantined, all from measurements/EP64_memphis_RAW.md. The earlier 122/109/17 was never measured.)

RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (was: ledger not written). The ledger is written from the 61,774-character opinion at measurements/EP64_memphis_RAW.md (CourtListener cluster 109855; 436 U.S. 1, filed 1978-05-01). THREE FINDINGS FROM THAT LEDGER BIND THE SCRIPT: (1) the opinion CONTRADICTS ITSELF on who failed to merge the accounts -- the majority says a contractor the Crafts hired, a footnote citing respondents' brief says the utility -- and on the number of terminations (majority: five; dissent: 'several'). The Court never resolved either, so the script may not pick a side. (2) NOBODY EVER DECIDED WHETHER THE CRAFTS OWED THE MONEY, so 'they were overcharged' is not available. (3) the Court expressly preserved the utility's power to cut service after a hearing. VERBATIM, checked against measurements/EP64_memphis_RAW.md on 2026-08-04: "And petitioners would retain the option to terminate service after affording this opportunity and concluding that the amount billed was justly due." (An earlier revision of this note printed "after affording the notice and hearing required" as if it were the Court's words. That string is NOT in the opinion -- it was a paraphrase carried over from a chat summary and written here as verbatim. Never quote from a summary.) -- so 'a hearing before shutoff' must never be told as 'shutoff was stopped'. Stevens's dissent is strong and quotable; use it so the film is not one-sided.

RETRIEVAL NOTE for anyone re-fetching: a plain search for 'Memphis Light' on the Supreme Court returns 408 results and NONE of them is this case — they are all later Tennessee workers-compensation matters. The query that works is the exact case name with the ampersand plus filed_after=1977 / filed_before=1979.

CourtListener's copy has no syllabus. If the episode needs one it must come from elsewhere.
